effect: The completed body shows how balance signals help steady the eyes during a head turn and contribute to posture alongside other information.
reaction: The opposite eye movement was a satisfying, clear payoff for connecting the pathways.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the balance pathways to the body was most worthwhile: the final picture showed what the assembled parts actually do for vision and posture.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the two finished balance organs was straightforward, but it added less explanation than building the individual sensors.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the eyes move opposite to a head turn to keep a view steadier. The weighted-membrane comparison also clarified the difference between starting to move and steady motion.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt clearly arbitrary. The pathway connections followed the pictures, although the intermediate nerve and reflex steps mainly showed where the routes went rather than explaining how the reflex works.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing the separate sensors connect to a familiar action was interesting, though the middle assembly steps were fairly predictable.
